Dictionary Search

This component offers searching for words matching a set of criteria, given by regular expressions. Some prior knowledge of regular expression syntax is expected of the user.

Basic usage

Any number of concurrent criteria can be set to filter the database. The + button adds a filter row, the − button deletes one (the last row cannot be deleted). The searched data sources are chosen in Settings, where several dictionaries can be switched on or off (English, Czech, periodic table of elements, Pokémon, Wordle); all toggled-on sources are searched at once and the filter menus offer the union of their constraint kinds. Words matching all of the expressions simultaneously will be sought. The regular expressions should not be enclosed between a pair of slashes (as is usual in some contexts). A toggle button next to each filter can be used to negate the action of the regular expression (i.e. to search for words not matching it). A filter with an empty value (or an impossible range) is ignored.

Constraint kinds

Each filter row has a constraint-type menu: contains (a free regular expression), starts with, ends with or equals (the whole normalized form). Depending on the chosen dictionary, further kinds are offered: between words and length for the word dictionaries, symbol and atomic number for the periodic table, type and Pokémon no. for Pokémon. Numeric kinds (length, atomic number, Pokémon no.) add an operator menu (=, <, >, <=, >= or a range between two values). The second value field is used by between words and by the from–to operator: it means every word between the first and the second word, in alphabetical order. A filter with an empty value (or an impossible range) is ignored.

The Yes/No toggle next to each filter inverts the criterion, i.e. it searches for words that do not satisfy it.

A reference view of the currently selected dictionary can be opened from the toolbar (the Reference action).

Regexp implementation

The regexp parser uses the PCRE (Perl-compatible regular expressions, see www.pcre.org) syntax. The options PCRE_UTF8 and PCRE_UCP are activated to allow for possible Unicode national characters and alter the behaviour of the [[:lower:]], [[:upper:]] etc. characters classes accordingly.

If the number of results is too large, only the first 10000 matches will be shown in the list. The Go button shows the first 201 matches; the Show all button repeats the same search and lists up to 10000 full records (each prefixed with its normalized form).

Format of the dictionary

Every entry of the dictionary follows the pattern:
 oneill:O\'Neill
The part preceding the colon is a word in a normalized form, i.e., containing only lowercase English letters. On the right-hand side of the colon, the same word is found in its full original form, which may contain capitals and/or apostrophes. It is possible to impose search criteria on either part, however, only the full form will be displayed in the search results.

Regular expression tips and tricks

To match the whole normalized form against an expression expr, use:
 ^expr:
To match the full form:
 :expr$
To search for a pattern within the normalized form:
 expr.*:
To search for a pattern within the full form:
 :.*expr

Examples of search criteria:

Words containing \"hey\":
 hey
Five-letter words whose first letter is K and fourth letter T:
 :k..t.$
Words beginning as well as ending with an \"ing\":
 ^ing.*ing:
Words composed of letters in the first row of a computer keyboard only:
 ^[qwertyuiop]*:
Words containing H at least three times:
 (h.*){3}:
Five-letter palindromes:
 :(.)(.).\\2\\1$
Textonyms of \"home\":
 ^[ghi][mno][mno][def]:

Examples of filters:

Exactly 7-letter words:
 ^.{7}:
Words at least 7 letters long:
 ^.{7,}: or .{7}:
Words beginning with a lowercase letter (excluding surnames, acronyms, etc.):
 :[a-z]
Only all-lowercase words, no apostrophe:
 :[a-z]*$ or (exclude) [[:upper:]\']
Words with no repeating letters:
 (exclude) (.).*\\1.*:
